assertions.title: Reported prompting effects on bias vary across models and bias categories
assertions.statement: The cited evaluations report that the effects of prompting-based bias mitigation vary across model conditions and bias categories.
assertions.label: Prompting-Effekte variieren nach Modell und Biasart

review.findings: Kaneko et al. state that CoT does not necessarily debias better than a debiasing prompt for relatively small or only pre-trained models, and Kamruzzaman and Kim state that the best combination of prompting features depends on the exact model and bias category. Together these support that effects vary across model conditions and bias categories, worded as reported by the cited evaluations. Each source supports one dimension and the combined wording stays hedged.

evidence.statement: Kamruzzaman and Kim report that the strongest prompting configuration is not universal across models and bias categories.
evidence.quote: the best combination of features depends on the exact model and bias category
evidence.title: Prompting Techniques for Reducing Social Bias in LLMs through System 1 and System 2 Cognitive Processes

review.findings: Read the abstract, dataset and experimental setup, model/bias-specific results, invalid-response handling and conclusion. The study compares 12 prompting configurations, five LLMs and nine bias categories on two benchmark datasets. The abstract quote is reproduced exactly and Results section 5 explicitly says the best configuration is not universal across models and categories. The result discussion also reports that CoT can increase stereotypical responses on average despite broader abstract wording; the distillate does not assert universal CoT benefit. Its limited configuration-dependence claim is supported. No practice effectiveness or study-quality approval is inferred.

evidence.statement: Kaneko et al. report that Chain-of-Thought does not consistently outperform a debiasing prompt for smaller or only pretrained models.
evidence.quote: for relatively small models or models that have only been pre-trained, CoT does not necessarily debias better than DP.
evidence.title: Evaluating Gender Bias in Large Language Models via Chain-of-Thought Prompting

review.findings: Read MGBR task definition, six prompt conditions, model settings, Table 1 and Results 3.3, downstream comparison 4.3, Conclusion, Limitations and Ethics Statement. The first quotation belongs to section 3.3, not 4.1; corrected the locator. Results support the reported direction of CoT bias-score reductions in the authors evaluation, while the table contains exceptions and section 4.3 expressly limits comparison with DP for smaller or only pretrained models. The distillate includes that qualification. The evidence is English binary-gender tasks and selected benchmarks, not established mitigation in social work, nonbinary populations or all models. Accepted for the narrow source-bound claims only.

The statement is limited to 'their evaluation' and 'measured bias scores', so it does not generalise beyond the reported setting.

assertions.title: Kabra et al. transfer reasoning traces through fine-tuning
assertions.statement: Kabra, Jha and Reddy define ReGiFT as a fine-tuning procedure that transfers reasoning traces generated by a reasoning model to base models as training supervision.
assertions.label: ReGiFT überträgt Reasoning durch Fine-Tuning

review.findings: The method section describes a two-step approach that extracts reasoning traces from advanced reasoning models and uses them to fine-tune base models, and names the result ReGiFT. The authors also contrast it with inference-time chain-of-thought prompting. The Statement describes the proposed procedure only and makes no effectiveness claim, in line with its scope boundary; the author names match the paper header.

evidence.statement: ReGiFT uses reasoning traces generated by a reasoning model as training supervision for base models; the transfer occurs through fine-tuning.
evidence.quote: we use these traces to fine-tune the base models
evidence.title: Reasoning Towards Fairness: Mitigating Bias in Language Models through Reasoning-Guided Fine-Tuning

review.findings: Accepted all three method statements and every quoted passage at its exact original-source locator: section 3 describes trace extraction followed by base-model fine-tuning; section 3.2 explicitly contrasts learned reasoning with inference-time CoT; section 4.1 reserves BBQ for evaluation. The broader method paragraph correctly names the trace model, SQuAD-v2, correct-final-answer selection and the three tested axes. Source footnote 2, Ethics/Limitations and visually inspected original Figures 1–4 support the stated boundaries; neither trace faithfulness, general efficacy, social-work transfer nor graph significance is asserted.
